input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: the wrapper now clears and reuses one statistics dict for every call instead of giving each call its own, so concurrent or nested calls of the same decorated function write into the same dict
- failure path: two threads (or two concurrent awaits of the async wrapper) call the same decorated function; the second call's stats.clear() wipes the first call's start_time and attempt_number, and both read a merged, wrong statistics view afterwards

Reviewer finding
- description: Overlapping invocations now share a mutable statistics dictionary, so their retry statistics interfere with each other.
- rationale: If two overlapping calls to the same async decorated function each fail once and then succeed, both retry copies update the same dictionary. Each call's initialization resets it and each retry increments its attempt count, allowing the final statistics to report three attempts although each call took only two. Previously, each invocation had its own statistics dictionary, keeping the exposed invocation's counts isolated.
critique: The finding names the same mechanism as the label: overlapping or concurrent calls to the same decorated function share one mutable statistics dict. One call's reset clobbers the other's state, and both counts merge into wrong attempt numbers. It also contrasts this with the previous behavior, where each call had its own dict.
